public_rationale: This is a conditional, necessity-style forecast with no deadline. Reliable agents in the real world will need common sense. It can only be scored once agents actually work reliably in the real world. The evidence I found says they do not yet. TheAgentCompany's best agent completed 30% of realistic workplace tasks (May 2025). On the Remote Labor Index, the best agent automated 2.5% of real freelance projects (October 2025). Because the antecedent has not happened, the claim cannot be scored as true or false.
limitations: Condition evidence runs only to October 2025. Later 2026 gains are unverified.
'Reliably' and 'common sense' have no agreed measures, so scoring would depend on interpretation even after the condition is met.

our_interpretation: I read this as a necessity claim about AI agents: if agents come to work reliably in real-world use, they will have had to gain commonsense competence about objects, people and entities.

Antecedent (condition): AI agents working reliably in real-world deployment, not just in demos. Reading: agents finish most realistic, end-to-end work tasks without human rescue, as shown by public evaluations.
The claim can only be tested once agents are reliable. Then one would check whether that reliability came with a recognised gain in commonsense reasoning.
criteria.support_condition: Agents become reliable in real-world use, and that reliability is clearly tied to a recognised advance in commonsense reasoning about objects, people and entities.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Agents become reliable in real-world use across broad tasks while still clearly lacking commonsense about objects, people and entities.
